original.title: Compare one-electron iron with a multi-electron oxidant titre
original.question: Can titration recover the five-to-one Fe(II)/permanganate electron ratio?
original.script:
# EC-009: Compare one-electron iron with a multi-electron oxidant titre
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 H2SO4 0.005mol
add v1 FeSO4 0.001mol
titrate v1 KMnO4 0.02M 0.1mL until colour persists max 200
measure v1 uvvis
inspect
original.expected_result: For the acidic Mn2+ endpoint, 1 mmol Fe(II) supplies the electrons for 0.2 mmol permanganate, nominally 10 mL titrant.

expected_processes.interpretation: Educational equation or schematic relationship; not a claim that every species, pathway or coupling is implemented.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Confirm Fe(II) loss, Fe(III) formation and the actual manganese endpoint.
Do not apply the 5:1 ratio if MnO2 or another manganese product dominates.

novelty.basis: A new experimental question or substantive controlled extension; not a novel scientific discovery or necessarily a new reaction family.
novelty.distinction: Introduces a ferrous-ion redox assay with different electron stoichiometry from oxalate standardisation.
novelty.original_147_note: Original catalogue reviewed as source context through web excerpts; no complete local automated comparison or semantic-novelty certification.

limitations: Air oxidation before titration and database redox ownership can bias the apparent titre.
original.safety_context: Simulation-only script. Not a wet-lab procedure, school risk assessment or permission to perform the chemistry.
original.importance_rationale: Upper-secondary quantitative reasoning or multistep experimental interpretation.
